articleTitle: Optimal Electric Vehicle Charging Station Placing with Integration of Renewable Energy
abstract: In light of the large-scale electric vehicle (EV) development which outnumber the public charging stations, it is imperative to design and locate electric vehicle charging station (EVCS) in order to deliver lower costs for both charging infrastructure owners and distribution grids. In this paper, we investigated the location problem of EVCSs on city-scale in a synergy between photovoltaic (PV) panels and the grid where budget constraint and cooperative covering of charging spots are considered. Based on the assignment rules of energy management for each charging station, a mixed integer linear model is developed to formulate the problem. This paper aims to combine modelling of the power consumption and production associated with both grid and renewable energies and maximization of EVCS profits, on the owner of charging station side. Applying the model to five charging station candidates in Mashhad, the results show that using this model and the simultaneous presence of EVs and renewable energy sources in the network, make a reduction in costs while an increase in profits.

articleTitle: Modeling a Multi-Objective Vehicle Routing Problem for Monetary Operation in the Banking System
abstract: One of the principal processes in the banking system is the transportation issues. The banking system networks consist of several treasuries and several branches that transfer their vehicles from the treasuries to the branches. The main features that are considered in the banking system include the monetary operation. The main activity in order to successfully process of remittance is vehicle routing so that it can perform the monetary operation in the shortest possible time with the least risk. In this research, a multi-objective model is proposed, aimed at reducing supply chain costs, reducing the delivery time and money transfers and related risk reduction. Vehicles play an effective role in the banking system, so vehicles are considered heterogeneous. The demand associated with the branch is assumed to be time-varying and deterministic. The proposed model is a mixed-integer linear program, which is a numerical example for solving and the validation study in medium size by using General Algebraic Modeling System (GAMS)software.

articleTitle: Investigating Green Human Resource Practices in the Healthcare Sector: A Joint Application of Balanced Scorecard and SIR Method
abstract: Today, human resources are the most important factor in organizations, and the “Green” concept has become important concept around the world. So, greening human capital of an organization can be an effective way for achieving green firm. The purpose of this study is introducing a conceptual modelling for investigating green practices in the base of human resources balanced scorecard (HRBSC) by using superiority and inferiority ranking (SIR) method. SIR is almost a new MCDM method, and by using this, we can obtain both partially and completely ranking faster. In this way, we extracted the most important green practices according to the literature, and also we used expert opinions from the healthcare system. As the result, the most key practices known as “green recruitment” and “environmental training”. Managers can turn hospital's culture into green and reduce environmental effects on the way of improving the healthcare system by the results.

articleTitle: Optimization and Coordination of a Sustainable Supply Chain with Emission Reduction Considerations
abstract: Low-Carbon supply chains have gained many attentions from academia, practitioners, governments and nongovernmental organizations. Along with that, the growing awareness of market about the carbon footprint of the produces that it consumes have led to the joint problem of sustainable supply chain coordination and emission abatement. Here a two-echelon supply chain, consisting a single retailer and a single manufacturer has been investigated in a Stackelberg game setting where the manufacturer is the channel leader. Implementing the consumer's green consumption preference and carbon abatement level into the demand function, a revenue sharing contract in been conducted to solve the channel conflict and double marginalization effect. The analytical results and numerical example prove the profit improvement of both channel members and validates the effectiveness and environmental-friendliness of the constructed settings.

articleTitle: The Location Allocation Problem of After Disaster Blood Supply Chain
abstract: In this paper blood supply chain planning in disaster situation is discussed. A new model for simultaneous midterm and short term planning is proposed in order to minimize the whole network's costs. Blood demand is considered as a stochastic phenomenon and a scenario based method is used to model this uncertainty. This model determines location of fixed blood centers which should be established after disaster (instead of centers that are ruined during the disaster)and location of mobile blood facilities (which can move in order to collect blood in each time period). Assignment of blood donors to fixed centers and mobile facilities and transportation plan for transferring blood from mobile facilities to fixed centers is also considered. The proposed model is solved using GAMS software for a case study.

articleTitle: Optimization of Preventive Maintenance Scheduling based on Monte Carlo Simulation in Processing Plants
abstract: The preventive maintenance is defined as a collection of activities aimed at improving the overall reliability and availability of the system. preventive maintenance schedule is a maintenance system is essential for manufacturing organizations in order to maintain competitiveness. The methodology is based on the use of a Monte Carlo simulation to calculated to determine the expected value of a random variable. The Monte Carlo simulation depict different failure models of equipment and uses the prioritization of maintenance supplied, the availability of labour and spare parts.

articleTitle: A New Fuzzy Approach for Project Time Assessment Under Uncertain Conditions
abstract: Project control is a part of feedback system intended to find and rectify deviations from desired plan. Earned value management (EVM) and its extensions as project control approaches regard monetary values to assess the project schedule performance. For this reason., they sometimes provide inaccurate duration performance results. In this regard, earned duration management (EDM) which is an effective project time control method, is proposed. EDM is a cost value free technique in evaluating and estimating the project time performance. Since the uncertainty is inherent in projects' areas, it should be considered in the control and monitoring process. In this paper, a new triangular intuitionistic fuzzy earned duration model is presented to control the project time performance under uncertain conditions. Modified EDM indices and measures are introduced to evaluate the project time performance under uncertainty. Finally, a case study from the recent literature about construction project is given to show the model's applicability in real-life conditions.

articleTitle: A Robust Optimization Model for Joint Maintenance and Build-To-Order Supply Chain Under Uncertainties: A Case Study
abstract: This paper proposed a new bi-objective supply chain model in a build-to-order (BTO)environment, which aims to maximize the profit and minimize the stops of devices by preventive maintenance. Maintenance is a new issue in BTO systems. In addition, due to the application of uncertain parameters and variables, the robust optimization model is used and implemented in a wood industry in order to validate this developed model.

articleTitle: Bottleneck Detection in Job Shop Production by High-Level Petri Nets
abstract: Bottlenecks are one of the most important problems that can effect the performance of the production systems. Detection of the bottlenecks in the production process can increase the performance of production system. This research is based on detecting bottlenecks by high-level petri nets in the job-shop production system. The capabilities of this method lead us to monitor the job-shop manufacturing process for avoiding of bottlenecks before running the system for evaluating time cycle production and reducing it by optimizing methods in the future works. The case study conducted at the Tarrah Sanaye Khouzestan industrial group placed at Albaji industrial zone, Ahvaz, Iran. The results showed the performance of high-level petri nets for detecting the bottlenecks and modeling the concurrent systems like job shop production systems.

articleTitle: Measuring the Waste Water in a Yoghurt Production Plant and Redesigning the Cleaning in Place Process (Case Study: Kalleh Dairy Factory)
abstract: In the background of world wild water scarcity, water conservation is appearing as an important indicator in the industry. Water, like energy, is a significant input into any economy. This paper provides a case study of a yoghurt plant in Kalleh dairy factory to access the material consumption through the cleaning in place process. The total consumptive material measured and a new structure for the cleaning in place tanks proposed. The current material consumption evaluated to the new design material usage. The results confirm that the yoghurt plant can preserve 8738100000 IRR per year utilizing recovery tank.

articleTitle: A Mathematical Model for Robust Facility Layout Problem in 3D Space with Possibility of Floors
abstract: The goal of any facility layout problem is proper arrangement of facilities without overlapping. Most of facility layout problems are two-dimensional and single-floor. In this study, facility layout problem is considered in three-dimensional and multi-floor. This will increase the flexibility of the problem. Also, many of layout problems are deterministic, while it is possible that parameters of the problem can be changeable. Therefore, robust planning should be used in overlapping constraints. We develop a mathematical model considering some flexible assumptions. In order to measure the validity of the model, we solve some examples using the appropriate software. Computational experiments show that the objective function of mathematical model increases by considering flexibility in parameters.

articleTitle: Stackelberg-Equilibrium of Pricing and Inventory Decisions in a Supply Chain
abstract: Pricing and inventory decisions are two important issues which directly affects the revenue and internal costs of a firm. Therefore, integrating these decisions would be of interest. In this paper, a supply chain with manufacturer-Stackelberg structure consisting of a manufacturer and a retailer is considered. The manufacturer offers the wholesale price to the retailer anticipating the retailer's response, while the retailer determines his optimal replenishment cycle and retail price simultaneously. We formulate the problems of both manufacturer and retailer, and characterize the Stackelberg-equilibrium assuming a linear demand model. Furthermore, a numerical experiment is carried out to investigate the sensitivity of the solution on the model parameters. Numerical results show that the retailer will benefit from a higher deterioration rate in the manufacturer-Stackelberg structure.

articleTitle: A Ship Routing and Scheduling Problem Considering Pickup and Delivery, Time Windows and Draft Limit
abstract: This article refers to the traveling salesman problem (TSP) that includes pickup and delivery the cargoes under two constraints, draft limit and time windows, which is an important issue in marine logistics, in which every node shows a port with a specific time window and draft limits. The demand for each port is different in receiving and delivering cargos, and these requests are carried by a single ship. The compatibility of the two parameters, the weight of the cargo and the port's draft, is necessary for a safe visit in the port. We presented a numerical example and compared the results of solving it in two ways: integer linear programming using GAMS software and forward dynamic programming, we analyzed the different states of movement of the ship and obtained the best possible route in order to minimize the cost and then we have showed the compatibility of these two methods.

articleTitle: Modeling the Problem of Operating Rooms and Different Wards of Health Centers Scheduling and Planning
abstract: Today, task scheduling is an important indicator in many vital decision-makings in the healthcare sectors. The tendency to make decisions with the aim to minimize the time spent doing things is among the reasons to propose scheduling problems. The proper scheduling will greatly reduce the organization's costs. Therefore, the scheduling usage of operating rooms is considered as an important issue. Accordingly, the current research proposes a model to schedule and plan all hospital wards with the aim to minimize task scheduling in healthcare centers. The innovation in this research is due to providing a model with regard to all constraints of healthcare centers, personnel, and patients, and attaining the intended time objectives of the healthcare centers. In addition, results obtained from solving this model using GAMS software and a set of random data have been logical and useful, indicating the performance improvement of different wards of hospital and patients' satisfaction.

articleTitle: A Proactive Approach to Evaluate Performance of BPEL Workflows by Queuing Theory and Stochastic Petri Net
abstract: Service oriented architecture is a novel paradigm for developing software based on composition of components or services. This innovation in the context of software engineering facilitates reusability of services according to loosely coupled relations. Meanwhile, BPEL standard accelerates composition of services. Although many efforts have been made to prove functional correctness of composed services through formal verification techniques, prediction of non-functional properties such as performance, reliability, and availability received less attention. Since BPEL service is similar to a workflow, it has been modeled with Stochastic Petri Net. We have extended SPN to fit our purpose. In this paper, we have presented an analytical modeling approach based on SPN where it uses a sequence of matrix calculations in a statistical space. The calculations are according to exponential distribution for transitions and Poisson distribution for arcs. Simulation results have validated the model for performance of a complex example. This approach can also be deployed for prediction of reliability and availability.

articleTitle: Improving the Value of Strategic Projects with Uncertainty and Flexibility: A Central Hospital Case Study
abstract: The design and evaluation of strategic projects can be very challenging tasks, as future changes in the design of these projects can be too expensive later on. The traditional engineering techniques for project evaluation do not take uncertainty into account, while there is a range of uncertainty resources in reality. In addition, they ignore the role of system operators throughout the project life time, whereas the intelligence of managers and decision-makers should not be underestimated. Hence, a four-step evaluation process based on simulation is proposed to solve the problem with uncertainty and flexibility, also known as real options. One of the challenges in Iran's healthcare system is a shortage of 70 to 80 thousands hospital beds due to the lack of government funding and investment. Study shows that it takes 35 to 40 years to meet the hospital needs while future can be quite uncertain and making the evaluation process challenging. To tackle this issue, there is a need to evaluate healthcare projects as accurate as possible by considering uncertainty and flexibility. For an example of how to deal with this challenge, to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed methodology, the design evaluation of a central hospital is investigated in this study.

articleTitle: Investigating the Effect of Global Brand on Willingness to Pay More by Mediation of Brand Perceived Quality, Brand Image, and Brand Prestige
abstract: Globalization of markets makes it more important than ever to understand the preference of global brands rather than local brands by some consumers. Furthermore, global branding, in addition to its many advantages for companies, makes them capable of creating a better image for their goods and services. This study examines how global brand may influence consumers' tendency to pay more, as mediated by brand perceived quality, brand image, and brand prestige. To do so, a library study was accomplished which its results revealed that there is a direct and positive connection between global brand and brand image. In addition, it is determined that global brand indirectly affects the tendency to pay more by mediation of brand perceived quality, brand image, and brand prestige. Finally, the conceptual framework is provided based on conducted investigations.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Double Variable Sampling Plan
abstract: Traditional double variable sampling plan is an inspection with crisp parameter, so that it is not able to make a decision about manufacturing products whose proportion parameter ( p) is uncertain. The major purpose of this study is to design double variable sampling plan when p is imprecise to inspect the lots of manufacturing products as interested characteristics are normally distributed. The plan parameters are obtained by optimization problem. During the process of solving optimization problem, sum of the fuzzy customer and producer's risks and contract's requirements are considered as objective function and constraints, respectively. The optimal parameters are prepared to use in industrial environments for various combinations of requirements. We indicate that the proposed scheme turns to classical one as p is not vague. The obtained results presents that the introduced scheme is more economical than the available plan. Finally, a practical example is presented in real applications.

articleTitle: Multi-Period Modular Capacitated Hub Location Problem with a Splittable Flow of Commodities and Multimodal Transportation System
abstract: This study examines a hub network design problem by applying commodity split, multimodal transportation system, and capacity modulation concepts to be significantly reduced the hub network costs. It also considers the possibility of transportation infrastructure establishment to be made the problem one step closer to reality. The results show that the application of multimodal transportation, capacity modulation, and commodity split concepts reduces the hub network costs.

articleTitle: GARCH Model-Based Fuzzy Clustering of Asian and Oceania Stock Markets
abstract: This paper applies fuzzy clustering based on partitioning around medoids algorithm to partition financial time series. To measure the similarity or dissimilarity between employed time series, GARCH parametric approach is exerted. Based on the fuzzy and crisp silhouette criteria, some main Asian and Oceania stock markets are partitioned in two (the best choice for number of) clusters. The results indicate that the stock market of Thailand, Taiwan, Singapore, Australia, India, Philippines, South korea, Hong kong, Indonesia and China have similar trend with high degree membership.

articleTitle: Improving the Mean Waiting Time of Patients by by Simulation in a Health Service Provision Clinic
abstract: In this paper, a reception model is proposed to improve waiting time of patients considering utilization of doctors and nurses in a neurology clinic by discrete-event simulation (DES). A neurology clinic including 8 doctors with different specialties is investigated. First, an interview and observation was done and then, required data relating patients' traffic were recorded and used for simulation. To analyze case study, first, bottlenecks were identified. It was observed that mean waiting time (MWT) of patients in total reception was high. For improving MWF, some scenarios were defined. Among all scenarios, increasing the number of nurses in the reception unit was the most effective one. The results of DES shows that by increasing the number of nurses to 4 individuals, the MWT can be decreased 8.345 minutes per day for each patient. Also, the utilization of doctors can be increased considerably. For validation, the results of the simulation were compared with real data by statistical analysis. These analysis approved the DES results.

articleTitle: Stabilization of Nonlinear Homogeneous and Cooperative Delay Systems
abstract: We review delay cooperative systems and define a proper stabilizing controller by considering the corresponding realtime systems. It is also proved that it has all the necessary and sufficient conditions for using the results of the recent studies in this area. In fact, we provide an analytical method which can simplify studying the stability of delay systems. Then the associated numerical results are presented.

articleTitle: A Two-Stage Stochastic Problem for Location & Allocation Model with Bernoulli Demands
abstract: In this paper, a new scenario reduction scheme is introduced to solve a two-stage stochastic program for location and allocation problem with Bernoulli demands. The location of facilities and the customer allocation are decided in the first stage. When the actual demand of customers is realized, second stage decisions are determined to serve customers. Each customer demand may get a 0 or 1 value with its own probability. Therefore, the number of scenarios increases exponentially while the number of customers grows. A model is formulated to decrease the number of scenarios. The validity of the proposed model is demonstrated by solving many instances in different sizes. The model has been examined with diverse numerical examples. Finally, it has been shown that the scenario reduction model has an effective performance in decreasing the solution time with an acceptable solution.

articleTitle: The Role of Knowledge Management in Improving the Staff Performance of a Set
abstract: Today, the most common model of attendance that can be seen in offices is the use of fingerprint attendance systems and, in particular, face detection systems. These systems always have problems. In this paper, in addition to covering the problems of these systems, a system for the automatic presence of individuals is presented, which, in addition to automatic attendance, can be used to measure the performance of a team at the end of the year. In fact, these systems are based on instantaneous locating systems. In addition, this paper attempts to overcome some problems in the area of overtime, such as the exact recording of the number of overtime hours per person, as well as the difficulty of resting people in overtime hours.

articleTitle: A Resilient Agribusiness Supply Chain Network Design in a Two-Stage Stochastic Programming Framework
abstract: Agribusiness supply chains are sensitive to various sources of uncertainty. Therefore, it is essential to consider resiliency for such supply chains to decrease the impacts of various types of risks. This article presents a two-stage stochastic model considering disruption scenarios for both suppliers and distribution centers to design resilient agro-food supply chain. To react quickly despite of any disruptive incidents, three following strategies are intended to develop a resilient model; 1)devoting backup facility to suppliers and distribution centers, 2)multiple-sourcing in suppliers and distribution centers, 3)mitigation strategies for suppliers to reduce the disruption probability. The model is solved using simulated data set and the results prove that implementing resilient strategies for mentioned supply chains will gain more profit and economize its costs. An analytical comparison between both classic and resilient models as well as analysis on wrong strategy selecting effect have been considered.

articleTitle: Introducing a Method for Combining Supervised and Semi-Supervised Methods in Fraud Detection
abstract: As electronic transactions are growing, fraud cases are also growing drastically. Detection of frauds is a complicated task and limiting fraud detection systems to certain kinds of detection methods like supervised or unsupervised methods does not seem efficient. In this paper, a combination framework for fraud detection systems, consisting of both supervised and semi-supervised methods in three main components namely rule-based component, trend-analysis-based component and, a scenario-based component is proposed. The rule-based component is the supervised part of the framework and decision tree which is a cost-insensitive classification algorithm is used for this component. In the trend-analysis-based component, which is the semi-supervised part of our proposed framework, the normal behavior of users are modeled and the extent of dissimilarities of newly-arrived transactions are calculated. Finally, in the scenario-based component which is another semi-supervised part of the proposed framework, the extent of similarities of the sequence of transactions to known fraud scenarios are calculated. The final result is gained through combining the results of all these three components using in a parallel mode. By combining the outputs of all these components together using the SUM function, the detection rate has increased remarkably (about 7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>).

articleTitle: Interpretive Structural Modeling Analysis of Reverse Supply Chain Critical Success Factors in Air Industry
abstract: The air industry is an integral part of the world economy. Based on this, understanding the key factors of success will create a competitive advantage and success in this industry. This research with Understanding the subject and identifying 159 factors by studying the literature of research, reached to 73 factors with an initial sieve. Ultimately, 24 critical success factors were identified by Lawshe technique and with the Structural Interpretative Modeling approach and utilizing experts' opinions we categorized the main success factors of the air industry. The results of the research show that the most influential factors are related to inventory management, transportation, materials and information integration, communications, information technology, mutual trust of supply chain partners, supply chain performance, supply chain flexibility, awareness of inverse support, Knowledge management, standardization, supply chain reliability, collection of return products, monitoring systems for return, cooperation of supply chain components, return and protection policies, and commitment of beneficiaries as interface factors which any partial changes on these factors leading to fundamental changes in the system.

articleTitle: A Multi-Agent Framework for Virtual Production System Considering Global Manufacturing Paradigm
abstract: In this paper a web based production system is proposed. This system consists of a web services agent to manage the receipt the order from the customer, a price agent to predict the price of the product for the customer, a decision agent to build up a virtual enterprise to manufacture and deliver of the product to the customer and make essential decisions of the system and a design and control agent to do the engineering tasks related to the production process of the product. This structure provides the production system with a high level of agility and flexibility.

articleTitle: Red Blood Cells Consumption: An Optimization Method
abstract: Optimal red blood cells (RBCs) consumption management as an invaluable product can contribute noticeably to communities' healthcare. Therefore, the main purpose of this research is to help the medical community and the human community in providing fast and timely blood products at the lowest cost. Blood products' life are taken into account since ordering policies are depended on the time of inventory. For each hospital, a new decision is made for RBCs production for the whole day. The decision-making process is repeated the next day with respect to the inventory status. Markov decision-making process is used as a decision-making tool for blood inventory problem. We used MATLAB 2016b software to solve the Markov decision-making for RBCs with sequential approximation algorithm. Real-life data are used to investigate the model. Obtained results after 278256 iterations show that 13.19%, 45.13% and 41.68% of costs are related to (LIFO-FIFO), (LIFO-LIFO)and (FIFO-FIFO)policies, respectively. By analyzing the different types of costs and comparing the policies, it is believed that (LIFO-LIFO)policy is better than other two policies and cumulated costs in this policy is lower than other ones in long time.

articleTitle: A Knowledge Oriented Framework to Enable New Service Development Using Axiomatic Design Theory: Focusing on Hotel Business Models
abstract: Although New Product Development and its application has been highly noticed, the New Service Development paradigm has been paid less attention yet. In this research, the new service development concept for Hotel industry is considered, validated and verified in a real hotel case. Axiomatic design theory is used to evaluate the required services. Customer domain is analyzed through a business model Canvas. This is accomplished through functional requirements analysis for a hotel and mapping them to generic services in market by assuring the feasibility and optimality of the system complexity. The required data for completing axiomatic design phases has been obtained through a knowledge based structure, which enable the business owners to manage data around the market. The results indicate the limited focus only on customer segment and also having no systematic approach for knowledge creation from data around business that are expected to be solved by the proposed framework.

articleTitle: Coordination of a Three-echelon Pharma-Supply Chain with Corporate Social Responsibility Under Spanning and Pair-wise Revenue Sharing Contracts
abstract: Expanding social dimensions of different businesses in the last decade's results in reviewing global issues in particular Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR). In this view, the achievement of desired responsibility levels is intertwined with classical decisions such as ordering and pricing. In addition, decision making processes in supply chains provides a range of theories and implications about conducting coordination mechanisms through the chain interactions. In this paper, a manufacturer, distributor and retailer are considered to form a three-echelon pharmaceutical supply chain. It is possible for the manufacturer to invest in responsibility level which improves market demand. Moreover, the demand depends on different prices which the retailer sets for end customers. Thus, the effect of pricing and responsibility levels on the profitability and coordination of the chain is analyses under different revenue sharing contracts. The coordination analysis shows that spanning revenue sharing can coordinate the chain partners in the absence of goodwill penalty costs where the holding costs should be assigned merely to one of the downstream partners. On the other hand the pair-wise revenue sharing cannot provide coordination condition and its level of efficiency is dependent on the Stackelberg gaming of the downstream partners.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Genetic and Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithms for Dynamic Facility Layout Problem with Multiple Transporters
abstract: Nowadays, manufacturing plants should be agile to changes their production mix plan based on dynamic demands. Here, layout design significantly could impact on manufacturing efficiency. When the flows of materials between departments embed variability during the planning horizon, this problem is known as the dynamic facility layout problem (DFLP). This paper extends such problem with considering multiple transporters, which commonly are used for transportation tasks among facilities. Hence, we extended the classical DFLP objective function in such a way that could encounter total combined rearrangement, material handling and transporting costs. Firstly, the relevant mathematical model is presented and then hybrid metaheuristic algorithms based on particle swarm optimization (PSO)and genetic algorithm (GA)presented to solve such problem efficiently. To achieve reliable results, a Taguchi's design of experiments is applied to calibrate initial parameters. Also, a few small-sized problems are solved using the CPLEX software. Analysis of the results shows that the proposed hybrid PSO algorithms have good solution quality according to the objective function and CPU time rather than hybrid GA and proved the effectiveness of this algorithm on the set of test problems.

articleTitle: Two-Machine Robotic Cell Scheduling with Controllable Inspection Times
abstract: This paper considers the stochastic scheduling of a two-machine robotic cell with controllable inspection times. The inspection is performed by a multi-function robot which performs the inspection of the part in transit between two machines. The robot cannot complete the part transition if it identifies a fault in the part. Instead, when the robot detects the fault, it moves back the source machine to reload the part. A characteristic of the inspection is that its required time is changed by altering the inspection cost. This generates a trade-off between the cost of quality and the partial cycle time. Initially, the cost of quality and cycle times of different partial cycles are derived based on a geometric distribution, and then the optimization problem is solved. Two versions of the problem are employed to minimize the expected cycle time or the expected cost of quality according to the concern of decision makers.

articleTitle: Designing a Bi-Objective Stochastic Blood Supply Chain Network in a Disaster
abstract: In spite of different advances in medicine, blood is still a limited source. As blood hasn't any chemical substitution that can be produced, managing its supply chain decisions to face minimum unmet demand level is vital. The problem becomes more complex by considering stochastic demands, blood product substitution and proportion of each blood group donors in population. Blood supply chain without considering donors, collection centers, hospitals and patients simultaneously is far from real world situations. In this study firstly we introduce a deterministic single objective linear programming then we convert the model to a bi-objective stochastic form to dealt with mentioned complexities. The bi-objective model seeks to optimize two conflicting objectives: the total supply chain cost and total shortages at different levels of supply chain. The presented model was solved by an Epsilon-Constraint method. The numerical and sensitivity analysis confirm the validity of proposed stochastic model.

articleTitle: Coordinating Replenishment Decisions in a Decentralized Two-Echelon Supply Chain Using by Revenue Sharing Contract
abstract: In recent years, coordination and participation in the supply chain have become one of the most important issues. The supply chain members, who are often independent entities, in order to deliver the products to the final consumer with the best quality and the shortest time, should cooperate with other members of the supply chain. In the investigated model, the stochastic demand in a decentralized supply chain is considered and the retailer uses Periodic Review Inventory System that the visit interval is determined by the supplier and he only decides on the service level that determining this amount can affect the supplier's profitability. Therefore, the supplier that has the full authority in determining the visit interval and the order delivery frequency, affects retailer inventory costs. In this paper, firstly decentralized and centralized supply chains are modelled and in order to coordinate the supply chain, the revenue sharing contract is used. Finally, with solve the numerical example, the results show that revenue sharing Contract can create coordination between supply chain's member and Therefore, the profits of them than operated independently increased and the supply chain becomes more efficient.

articleTitle: A Model to Promote Productivity for Knowledge Acquisition in Organizations
abstract: Knowledge acquisition is considered to be one of the important processes of knowledge management in organizations. In order to achieve the best knowledge acquisition productivity, it is essential that the resources of the organization be devoted in such a way that it will bring the organization most efficiency. Therefore, in order to select the necessary and necessary knowledge of the organization, first, it needs to be measured, and then these kinds of knowledge must be prioritized. Taking into account the opportunities and threats faced by the organization, the sources of funding for the most prioritized knowledge are chosen. For this purpose, using the SWOT matrix and AHP method, a model is proposed that allows the effective use of resources for knowledge acquisition in the organization. Meanwhile, the results of the implementation of this model in the pottery industry have been investigated.

articleTitle: Evaluating and Ranking Suppliers by a Multi-Attribute Decision Making Approach Under Uncertainty (Case Study: Steel Industry)
abstract: Deciding to choose a supplier is a key issue that has become a strategic goal for organizations in recent years. because of the diversity and variety of quality and quantity indicators, this decision making issue is considered as a Multi Attribute Decision Making problem. To do this, in the real world due to imprecise information, decision making is based on inaccurate information and linguistic terms; In this paper, a hybrid model of fuzzy analytical hierarchy process (FAHP)and fuzzy topsis method is presented, in the steel industry. In the first part of this model, after selecting the effective criteria and sub-criteria, in the steel industry, by using expert opinions, FAHP is used to extract the weights of the criteria and sub-criteria. In the second part of the model, the output weights of the previous stage are placed as inputs data and suppliers are ranked by Fuzzy Topsis Technique.

articleTitle: Designing a Conceptual Model for People's Participation in Resistive Economy: Text Grounded Theory Approach Based on Islamic Thoughts
abstract: The concept of Resistive Economy was first proposed by the Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic of Iran in 2010. Iran's current situation renders efforts for materialisation of its economy more vital today than ever. Humanization of the economy is one of the main pillars of resistive economy. In Islam, nobility is an attribute of both the individual and the society whereas in the western viewpoint, either the individual or the society is deemed noble. Based on this viewpoint, people of the country are expected to employ their full power to fulfill collective and national objectives under harsh circumstances such as sanctions and war. In such framework, notions such as resistance find meaning as one of the main pillars of resistive economy and virtues like plurality, dedication, devotion, helping fellows and the other necessary components of resistive economy should be realised. The current study aims to highlight the role of people in resistive economy based on fundamental values extracted from direct Islamic thoughts and guidance of the Supreme Leader by applying text analysis in grounded theory as the analysis tool. In spite of the variety of resources and diverse Islamic books available, researchers in the field have opted to emphasize on direct Islamic thoughts narrated in the Quran and Nahj al-Balaqa (the Pearls of Eloquence) in order to achieve a people-centered economic theory. These are the most complete available sources for practical guidelines and most advanced present human civilization. Moreover, given the Supreme Leader's knowledge and comprehensive insight into the field, as implemented in the current situation of the country, and given the requirements of an Islamic-Iranian lifestyle Ayatollah Khamenei's words in recent years are also used as an additional source of data in the study. Once the problem is coded and the data is analysed, a conceptual model for people's participation in the Iranian economy is illustrated.

articleTitle: A Multi-Objective Model for Optimizing Iranian Bank Portfolio Investment Considering Resistive Economy Criteria
abstract: One of the best components for economic growth is supporting national production, however, the main concerns of the manufacturing sector are easy and cheap financing that In Iran is carried out by the banking system, but since start of sanctions against Iran, because of high inflation, banks have turned to corporation and investment to increase their profits. Increase of economy's resistance against the menace of shocks and threats are one of the main national policies which can be satisfied through bank investments. In this research, a multi-objective and mixed integer programming model is proposed to determine the amount of bank investment in different domains and selecting the proposed projects, so that, while satisfying the banking policies (maximizing profit and minimizing risk), resistive economy policies is also realized. The results of the experiments show the necessity and importance of considering the components of the resistance economy in choosing investment projects.

Author Keywords: multi-objective and mixed integer programming model

articleTitle: The Impact of Brand Equity on Customer Equity
abstract: Brand equity (BE) and customer equity (CE) are the key concepts in marketing research. Although, less attention has been paid to the link between BE and CE. This research presents a conceptual framework for studying the relationship among the BE key components (knowledge, relevance, esteem, differentiation) and the CE key components or customer lifetime value (customer acquisition, share of wallet), which has been specifically examined in the elevator industry. This research also examines the role of marketing activities (advertising, discounts, and free consulting services) in this relationship. The data were gathered from a set of completed questionnaires and analyzed using linear regression and logistic regression. The results indicate significant effect of brand knowledge and differentiation on acquisition and share of wallet for existing customers and prospects. Findings also illustrate the positive effect of marketing activities, especially advertising and free consulting services on brand knowledge and differentiation.

articleTitle: The Appropriate Criteria for Selecting Indicators of Intellectual Capitals Measurement
abstract: Most organizations which reported their intellectual capital, have been suffering from numerous indicators for measuring it. This article developed a guide for selecting IC measurement indicators or developing needed metrics efficiently in accordance with an industry or organization requirement. The purpose of this article is identifying and determining features and requirements of intellectual capital measurements' indicators. Based on context literature related to intellectual capital and performance measurement, features and requirements of intellectual capital measurements' indicators were extracted and through benefiting from the experts and applying delphi method to them, the appropriate criteria for selecting indicators of intellectual capitals measurement was determined. The main finding of this study is a list of 11 criteria including 2 macro criteria and 9 main criteria for selecting indicators of intellectual capitals measurement.

articleTitle: Utilizing a Simulation Approach for Analysis of Patient Flow in the Emergency Department: A Case Study
abstract: Simulation has been shown to be one of the most powerful tools in many areas of the health-care system, a system which attracted the attention of researchers due to its intricacy. The main goal of this study is to evaluate the patients' flow in an emergency department (ED). Discrete event simulation (DES)has been used as the core of this research so that it offers various ways to reduce the length of stay (LOS)of patients in different segments of ED by assessing various scenarios. In particular, a new approach for verification of the simulated model will be discussed. This study reports on the results that extracted from a case study on patient record data in one of the EDs located in Tehran province. With the goal of verifying and validating the constructed model, a simulation has been done using Simulink from MATLAB software.

articleTitle: Designing of a Mushroom Supply Chain with Price Dependent Demand in a Sustainable Environment
abstract: Mushroom industry is one of the agri-food industries, which has a fair potential in some countries to make economic profits and care about social and environmental concerns. In this paper, the pricing and sustainability issues according to the deterministic and stochastic closed-loop supply chain of mushroom industry are studied. To do so, by proposing a mathematical multi-objective model and considering the social dimensions in modelling, the profit and environmental effects are respectively maximized and minimized at strategic and tactical levels. Using a case study mushroom company's data and stochastic programming method, and applying an improved version of the augmented ε-constraint method (AUGMECON2), the problem simultaneously optimizes the relevant objectives with different solution methods in fortuitous conditions.

articleTitle: Solving a Single-Server Parallel Machine Problem with Preventive Maintenances Using a Hyper-Heuristic Algorithm
abstract: This paper considers a parallel machine problem subject to a single server, machine unavailability due to preventive maintenances, setup times and release dates. The goal is to minimize the makespan and the total idle times, simultaneously. Since this special case of parallel machine is known to be NP-hard, a hyper-heuristic method is proposed to solve the model. The hyper-heuristic has two levels; on the lower level, a set of well-known algorithms in scheduling is defined. The selection policy is presented in the upper level where, considering the convergence and diversity of the current solutions, the most appropriate algorithm is chosen from the toolbox. The advantage of a hyper-heuristic lies in its flexibility in switching between different methods to improve the exploration and exploitation of the overall procedure. The proposed hyper-heuristic is validated and tested on different problem scales and the results emphasize its high precision and rapid convergence.

articleTitle: Dynamic Modeling of the Relationship Between Risks of Activities and Reduction of Activities Time in the Post-Implementation Phase of the Enterprise Resource Planning System Using Fuzzy Cognitive Maps
abstract: In recent years Many Iranian organizations have used ERP systems to improve the performance and effectiveness of their organizational activities, while very few of them have gained sustainable advantages of this system. One of those benefits is reducing of cycle time of production and one of the factors that reduces the cycle time of production is to reduce the time of activities. The successful implementation of an ERP system is just the first step in achieving a successful system and its sustainable advantages depend on continuous support, maintenance and upgrade of the system in the exploitation or post implementation phase. The post implementation phase is exactly where real challenges begin and many dangerous risks are likely to occur. In this study, the relationship between the risks of activities and the time of activities in post-implementation phase is dynamically modelled using Fuzzy Cognitive Maps. The main advantage of fuzzy cognitive map is its ability to model complex phenomena based on expert perceptions. This tool modeling related and uncertain events by imitation of human reasoning. For this purpose, 36 risks were identified and collected and categorized into 5 groups of user, technical, managerial, operational and external risks, and their relationships between them and reduction of time of activities were modelled. According to the findings of this study, managerial risks had the greatest impact on other system risks and output.

articleTitle: The Consideration of Job Satisfaction Among Shahid Hasheminejad Gas Refinery Company Employees
abstract: The aim of this study which is performed by supporting of Shahid Hasheminejad Gas Refinery Company, was to evaluate the state of job satisfaction and its indicators among its employees. In first phase, the developed questionnaires were distributed among staffs. After analyzing the questionnaire's data, the indicators which had the most and the least affection on the job satisfaction were determined. In the second phase, the indicators which had the most affection on the job satisfaction of employee were prioritized, using group FAHP method and three dimension harmonic gap-capability-influencing matrix. The findings in the first phase, showed that recognition, career promotion, equality, facilities, job security, evaluation and salary and fringes were the effective job satisfaction factors. In the second phase, salary and fringes were recognized as the most important factor on job satisfaction reduction of the employees.

articleTitle: A Model for Improving Recommender Systems Based on the Similarity of Users
abstract: Todays, regarding the information overload on the web, providing services to enhance network efficiency by using computer-based recommender systems has become a necessity. Naturally, these systems are unable to provide recommendations without the appropriate information. Therefore, the accuracy of the recommendation in the recommender systems is one of their main challenges. Hence, the purpose of this study is to provide a model for increasing the accuracy of recommender systems using two commonly used methods in recommendatory systems (clustering algorithm and associative rules)based on the possible similarity of users using Pearson Correlation Coefficient and the Crisp method. The data used to carry out this research is taken from the MovieLens site. The K-means algorithm was used for clustering, and the Apriori algorithm was used to extract rules for films and to determine the degree of films' dependency. The results indicated that the proposed model was more accurate than previous models.
